<reason>Both sides were sharp and stylish, but B built the cleaner decision rule and held it: a dating app's bans are theater unless they attach to a person, and the status quo offers nothing the morning after. B extracted a real concession under pressure — A admitted the per-account price rises and only replied that industry amortizes it — and converted that into "then the argument is about how many disposable accounts, and the answer is fewer." B also answered A's best pressure question honestly and directly (yes, slower and less anonymous as written; document variety and appeal are implementation quality, not a retreat), which defused A's strongest procedural attack that PRO was rewriting the motion. A's counter that verification only yields "a false lead to an innocent" was overstated and B punctured it: a liveness check still puts a real face, a document theft, and a payment trail on file versus a burner Gmail. A's live routes — the honeypot/leak risk to vulnerable users, exclusion of trans and immigrant users, and the fact that a retained file does not "unsend the transfer or walk you home" — remained partly alive and were vividly framed ("cargo-cult security"), but B's retention-versus-verification split and "she is already exposed to whoever she meets" blunted them, while B's "pick one" catch on the impatience/moral-hazard tension was only weakly patched by A's "different people, different moments." A's answer naming four existing friction mechanisms was its best moment, but B's closing reply — every item on that list is re-purchasable at a corner shop, a face is not — landed as the more memorable crystallization. B's clipped closing is a real execution cost, though it lost only its final clause.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>B's pressure question demanding a mechanism that stops a banned abuser returning the same evening, followed by B's closing reduction of A's answer (SIMs, handsets, re-cropped photos, prepaid cards) to "a toll booth costing about the price of dinner," while a face is the one credential you cannot restock.</best_rebuttal>
